(1) old subjects showed increased activity compared to young subjects in a frontoparial network during mental rotation, (2) this activity was not sufficient to maintain the same performance as young subjects and (3) increased activity in left lingua gyrus predicted performance in old subjects.
older adults show increased neural activity in a frontoparital network and additional areas, when performing a visuospatial task.

(i) older subjects activate a broader network of brain areas when performing a demanding cognitive task and (ii) they are able to modulate activity within this network with increasing task complexity, (iii) but not when postural control is required, (iv) and that (v) the left lingual gyrushows a high correlation with mental rotation performance under increased posturo-cognitive load.
In summary, our research is concerned with
age-related changes of the neural correlates of cognitive performance in a posturally demanding situation.
the identification of neural correlates of cognitive performance in older adults when postural load is increased.
the question how aging influences the neural mechanisms underlying cognitive performance under postural load.

the older subjects' ability to modulate BOLD response in the left lingual gyrushelps to maintain mental rotation performance under increased postual load.
